Let
\[
x=\frac{d_1}{d_2},\qquad y=\frac{d_2}{d_3}.
\]
Each \(A_k\) has one \(2\times2\) coupled block and one scalar entry. For a positive \(2\times2\) matrix with eigenvalues \(\mu_+\ge \mu_-\), if
\[
R=\frac{\mu_++\mu_-}{\sqrt{\mu_+\mu_-}},
\]
then
\[
\frac{\mu_+}{\mu_-}=K
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\sqrt K+\frac1{\sqrt K}=R.
\]

For the three coupled blocks, direct trace/determinant calculation gives
\[
R_1=\frac{x+4/x}{\sqrt3},\qquad
R_2=\frac{y+16/y}{2\sqrt3},\qquad
R_3=\frac{4xy+1/(xy)}{\sqrt3}.
\]
So if all block condition numbers are at most \(K\), and
\[
S=\sqrt3\left(\sqrt K+\frac1{\sqrt K}\right),
\]
then
\[
x+\frac4x\le S,\qquad
\frac{y+16/y}{2}\le S,\qquad
4xy+\frac1{xy}\le S.
\]

For fixed \(S\ge4\), write
\[
a=\frac{S-\sqrt{S^2-16}}2.
\]
Then the first two inequalities force
\[
x\ge a,\qquad y\ge 2a,
\]
while the third forces
\[
xy\le \frac1a,
\]
because the larger root of \(4z+1/z=S\) is \(1/a\). Hence feasibility requires
\[
2a^2\le \frac1a,
\]
or
\[
a\le 2^{-1/3}.
\]
The smallest possible \(S\) therefore occurs at
\[
a=2^{-1/3}.
\]
Then
\[
S=a+\frac4a
=2^{-1/3}+2^{7/3}
=2\left(2^{4/3}+2^{-4/3}\right)
=2H.
\]
Thus the optimal value satisfies
\[
\sqrt{\mathcal K_*}+\frac1{\sqrt{\mathcal K_*}}
=\frac{2H}{\sqrt3}.
\]
Solving for \(\sqrt{\mathcal K_*}>1\),
\[
\sqrt{\mathcal K_*}
=\frac{H+\sqrt{H^2-3}}{\sqrt3},
\]
so
\[
\mathcal K_*=\frac{(H+\sqrt{H^2-3})^2}{3}.
\]

Equality in the feasibility argument forces
\[
x=2^{-1/3},\qquad y=2^{2/3}.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{d_1}{d_2}=2^{-1/3},\qquad \frac{d_2}{d_3}=2^{2/3},
\]
so the unique scaling class is
\[
d_1:d_2:d_3=2^{1/3}:2^{2/3}:1.
\]

The scalar eigenvalue in each \(DA_kD\) lies between the two block eigenvalues at this scaling, so the full \(3\times3\) condition numbers are exactly the block condition numbers.

\[
\boxed{\left(\frac{(H+\sqrt{H^2-3})^2}{3},\ \sqrt[3]{2}:\sqrt[3]{4}:1\right)}
\]
